create.name: Nur Ashki Jerrahi Community (The Sufi Lodge)
create.bio:
The Nur Ashki Jerrahi Community is a Sufi order in the Halveti-Jerrahi line, whose founding pir, Muhammad Nureddin Jerrahi, was born in Istanbul in 1678. Shaykh Muzaffer Ozak, a later successor in that chain, brought the lineage to New York and in 1980 passed its transmission to Fariha al-Jerrahi and Lex Hixon, known as Shaykh Nur. Fariha has guided the community since his death. Its emphasis falls on love and the remembrance of God within a broad, open-hearted reading of Islam, and seekers of every religious path are welcome.

The community gathers at Dergah al-Farah, known as The Sufi Lodge, in Tribeca in Lower Manhattan, which also houses Pir Press and an archive foundation; its ceremony of zikr there welcomes the public on alternate Thursdays, with a reply needed by email first. Circles founded by Shaykh Nur and Shaykha Fariha meet in other American cities and in Mexico, Australia and the UK. The website shares teachings on Sufi meditation, the dervish path and the basics of prayer, and the YouTube channel carries Shaykha Fariha's weekly Friday khutbas along with recorded lectures on Ibn Arabi.

free_resources.title: Zikr at Dergah al-Farah / The Sufi Lodge
free_resources.description: The community's ceremony of remembrance at its Tribeca lodge, held for the public on alternate Thursdays; visitors reply by email beforehand and check the calendar for dates.

free_resources.title: Sufi Meditation
free_resources.description: A four-part teaching on meditation from Shaykh Nur al-Jerrahi, with readings by Shaykha Fariha, published on the community's site.

free_resources.title: Teachings
free_resources.description: The community's library of written teachings: Basics in Salat, Invitation to Union, The Dervish Path, a book of salawat prayers and Three Days of Prayer, among others.
